inputs.original_text: ISRAEL’S parliament began a debate today on a Bill that would make the death penalty the default punishment for West Bank Palestinians convicted of murdering Israelis. The Bill’s passage would be a victory for Israel’s far-right Minister of National Security Itamar Ben-Gvir, leader of the religious party that introduced the legislation. Opponents of the legislation call it racist, draconian and unlikely to deter attacks by Palestinian militants.
inputs.modified_text: They’ve started debating a bill that would make death the default punishment for West Bank Palestinians convicted of murdering Israelis. Don’t mistake the security talk for the real purpose: this looks like a way to hard-wire unequal justice into the system and make state power seem normal. Ben-Gvir’s religious party introduced it, and passage would be a political win for him. The claims that it will deter attacks are convenient cover; even the bill’s opponents say it is racist, draconian and unlikely to work. The debate itself helps make an extreme measure look like ordinary policy.
